the mechanisms that control secretion of the egg-laying hormone from the neuroendocrine bag cell neurons in the mollusk Aplysia californica.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bag cell neuron is a model system that is well suited for studying the role of Ca2+ from intracellular stores in the regulation of peptide secretion.
Ca2+ influx through voltage-gated calcium channels is the major trigger for neuroendocrine secretion from bag cell neurons, but that mitochondrial Ca2+ can also initiate this process.
the bag cell neurons have a very high threshold for peptide release, requiring both high Ca(2+) and a long stimulus.

mitochondrial Ca(2+)-dependent secretion is a novel mechanism of neuroendocrine signaling that may have broad implications for other neuroendocrine cells.
